analysis: Examined the new .github/workflows/ci-dev-hourly.yml (lines 1-38), the changelog fragment, and the docs/developer/build.md additions (head lines 340-356). The workflow is a scheduled and manually dispatchable job on ubuntu-24.04. Top-level permissions are {}. The job gets only actions: write and contents: read via the default GITHUB_TOKEN. It has no checkout and runs no PR-controlled code. The only expression interpolations are github.token and github.repository, both passed via env rather than inlined into the shell script, so there is no script-injection vector. The script calls gh api to list workflow_dispatch runs of ci-dev.yml on dev, skips if any is unfinished, and otherwise runs gh workflow run ci-dev.yml --ref dev. workflow_dispatch on this file is available only to users with write access, and the scheduled run needs the default branch. The jq output is only html_urls from the repository's own API, echoed in a notice. The hourly full run consumes CI minutes (macOS runners, possibly Darkbloom Sandbox routing), so overlap is limited by the unfinished-run check; this is a cost/availability matter and not part of the provider threat model. There is no change to provider code, coordinator-provider protocol, attestation, keys, cache or fan helper, so no threat-model assets (A-001..A-020) or boundaries (TB-002..TB-014) are affected. Remaining unverified contract: dev's ci-dev.yml must accept workflow_dispatch and issue creation for 'Hourly full dev CI failures' uses permissions not granted here. That lives in dev, outside the supplied evidence, and the docs note that a missing trigger fails with HTTP 422. A minor race window exists between the check and the dispatch, which is harmless. No security regression identified.
